messages:
matt: Quick heads-up — kicked off a small canary of the new Karpenter provisioner for GPU nodepool in us-west-2, focused on batch/rl workloads. Observed a few oddities during scale-up and drain.

julia: What oddities?

matt: Two things: (1) slow pod scheduling while Karpenter is creating GPU instances (~90–120s) even though ASG-based nodes were ~40s, (2) when we cordon+drain, pods land Pending for a long time due to GPU resource packing + nodeSelector constraints.

sam: Did you check node templates and taints? We added a gpu: true taint for isolation last week.

matt: Yes. Taint is fine. The real culprit seems to be the combination of pod anti-affinity + strict nodeSelector + instance type diversity (g4dn/g5a). Karpenter is launching mixed types and the scheduler prefers exact matches.

kai: Can you paste the provisioner snippet you used?

matt: Sure — simplified:

```
apiVersion: karpenter.sh/v1alpha5
kind: Provisioner
metadata:
  name: gpu-provisioner-canary
spec:
  requirements:
  - key: "node.kubernetes.io/instance-type"
    operator: In
    values: ["g5.2xlarge", "g4dn.xlarge"]
  taints:
  - key: "gpu"
    value: "true"
    effect: "NoSchedule"
  limits:
    resources:
      cpu: "2000"
      memory: "1Ti"
  consolidation: true
  ttlSecondsAfterEmpty: 300
```

julia: Hmm we enabled consolidation + short TTL — might be causing churn and some pods getting bounced. Consolidation is aggressive for GPU workloads where startup is slower.

irina: Also watch for ENI/IP limits per instance family in us-west-2 — hitting IP limits will make pods unschedulable even if instance is up.

matt: Good call. I saw this in the kubelet logs: `failed to add pod to network: unable to allocate IP: ENI limit reached` around the same time.

sam: For GPUs we should probably: disable consolidation for the gpu provisioner, increase ttlSecondsAfterEmpty to 900–1800, and set allowedInstanceTypes to a narrower set so packing is predictable.

kai: Agreed. Also consider `labels` and `nodeSelector` changes — use `karpenter.sh/capacity-type: spot` as an opt-in label rather than mixing in the same provisioner, so we can fallback to on-demand during interruptions.

julia: What about spot interruption handling? We saw one spot interrupt earlier and pods got evicted without graceful fallback. Ops-bot, do we have a policy hooked into node termination webhook?

ops-bot: Reminder: node termination handler is running in prod clusters. For canaries it was disabled by default in the test namespace.

matt: That explains it. I want to avoid user-facing OOM/evictions. Plan for next steps:
- Turn off consolidation on gpu-provisioner-canary
- Increase TTL to 1200
- Narrow instance family to g5.* only for this test
- Re-enable node termination handler and add a short pre-drain hook to prefer rescheduling to existing GPU nodes with free slots

irina: Also, add a probe for ENI exhaustion in the autoscaler alerts. We saw a spike in IP allocation failures during heavy scale-ups.

sam: Can we run a synthetic scale test: 30 pending pods that request full GPUs to force worst-case packing? Use the same affinity rules as RL jobs. I can script that.

matt: Please do. Also include a run where one of the g5 types is throttled (simulated spot interruption) to verify fallback.

kai: When you flip consolidation off, watch cost — consolidation kills idle nodes which saves money. We should measure cost delta for a week before deciding default.

julia: Agreed — add a Canary dashboard: pod pending time, node creation latency, ENI errors, spot interrupt rate, cost per GPU-hour.

matt: I'll update provisioner YAML and post results here after the next run. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

sam: If anyone wants to replicate the script: `kubectl run --image=busybox scale-gpu-test --replicas=30 -- sleep 1d --overrides='{"spec":{"containers":[{"name":"c","resources":{"limits":{"nvidia.com/gpu":"1"}}}]}}'` — rough, but works.

irina: Nice. Let's also add a note in the migration doc about region constraints: us-west-2 has fewer g5 spare capacity; consider us-east-1 for larger scale tests.

matt: noted. Last note: avoid changing both instance families and consolidation at same time — we'll do one variable per run.

ops-bot: Deploy checklist: `1) update provisioner yaml 2) enable node termination handler 3) update alerts 4) run synthetic scale test 5) collect metrics`

matt: OK kicking off changes in ~10m. Will update thread.
